Prospective Graduate Students
The Univeristy of Utah Geology and Geophsyics Department
Choose your path
GEOLOGY
M.S or Ph.D
GEOPHYSICS
M.S or Ph.D
GEOLOGICAL ENGINEERING
M.S, Ph.D or M.E (non-thesis)
Geology - Emphasises in the Earth’s composition (minerals & rocks), dynamic structure (faults,
folds & plate tectonics) and long history (as displayed in the succession of rock
units and the fossil record of life through time).
Geophysics - Emphasises the Earth’s deep interior by studying natural physical fields within
the Earth (gravity, magnetic, thermal and electrical fields) and the transfer of energy
throughout the Earth’s interior (seismic waves generated by earthquakes).
Geological Engineering - An engineering approach to solving important problems related to geological hazards
(such as earthquakes and landslides) and natural resources (such as surface water
and groundwater).
Degree Requirements
Masters Degree Requirements
Typically a 2 year program
At least 20 graduate level credit hours (5000, 6000, 7000)
At least 10 credit hours of thesis research
Complete Thesis w/Defense
Maintain 3.0 GPA
PhD Degree Requirements
a 3-5 year program
You, your faculty advisor & committee will decide if you need to take any graduate
level credit hours
At least 12 credit hours of thesis research
Pass PhD Qualifying Exam
Complete Dissertation w/ Defense
Maintain 3.0 GPA
Direct to PhD Degree Requirements
Typically a 5 year program
At least 20 graduate level credit hours (5000, 6000, 7000)
At least 12 credit hours of thesis research
Pass PhD Qualifying Exam
Complete Dissertation w/ Defense
Maintain 3.0 GPA
Important to note:
Most student who don’t have their master’s yet and want to do Direct to PhD, don’t
end up taking this route.
Instead, faculty will have a student start in a master’s program and then do a change
in grad classification a year and a half into their program
Masters of Engineering (M.E) Degree Requirements
Typically a 2 year program
At least 20 graduate level credit hours in major area
At least 10 graduate level redit hours in minor area
Complete a 1 semester research project
Maintain 3.0 GPA
Important to note:
M.E Students do not receive department funding.
When applying for the M.E program, students do not need to list 3 faculty of choice.
What you need to know
Funding
Once accepted into our program, our students are fully funded; meaning their general
graduate tuition and mandatory fees are covered.
Graduate students will receive funding through their participation as a Research Assistant,
Teaching Assistant (TBP), or by receiving a fellowship. Students do not need to apply
upfront for these.
Additional fees, such as differential fees or semester international fees, are not
covered by this and it is the student’s responsibility to pay for these.
International fees MAY be covered by a student’s faculty advisor, but that is a conversation
the student needs to have with them each semester.
Students will also get a ‘stipend’ or ‘allowance’. These are monthly payments if you
are a research or teaching assistant and a 1 time semester payment if you are on a
fellowship.
Visit this website for more information on the Tuition Benefit Program (TBP).
Health Insurance
All graduate students are eligible for health insurance through the university, at
no additional cost. More information is available on the Graduate School website.
Application Fee Waivers
We offer application fee waivers to students who have financial limitation.
Once you have communicated with a faculty advisor, they have agreed to review your
application, and have confirmed that they will pay the fee, you may email the graduate
advisor to request the waiver code; please cc the faculty member on your email.
Please note that there is no way to do a refund for the application fee if you have
a waiver code and it is not used.
International Students
International Students must meet U of U application deadlines and I-20 document deadlines.
International Students & Scholar Services: The International Student & Scholar Services office serves as the primary campus contact
for international students, scholars, and alumni.
Email: international@utah.edu
International Graduate Student Admissions
Email: iao@sa.utah.edu

APPLICATION STEPS
Before You Apply
Applying
After Applying
Once Accepted
Before Applying
Important Things to Know
Students who have identified and contacted their top faculty choices are more likely
to be accepted into a graduate program.
The majority of our students are admitted for Fall Semester.
GRE scores are no longer required.
There are no prerequisites to apply to our graduate programs.
Step 1. Search Faculty Directory
Search through our faculty directoryand the research themes and program page to find out which of our academic or research faculty aligns with your research interests.
(Note: The majority of our advising faculty are academic faculty.)
Step 2. Identify Faculty Advisor(s)
Prior to submitting an application, identify 3 potential advising faculty in our department.
Step 3. Contact Potential Advisor(s)
Contact the faculty member(s) directly with the following information:
Include your CV
Briefly introduce yourself, your background, and any connections you may have to them.
Briefly tell them about your experience and how your intrests are relevant to their research.
Do your research BEFORE sending an email.
Know about their research and publications
Share what interests you about their work
Give specifics when referring to their work
Inquire about openings on their current research project.
Important tips to follow:
Be personalbe and use your own words.
Be patient & understanding. If faculty don't respond to your emails, it is because
they are busy teaching, doing research, and advising students. They receive a lot
of prospective student requets and may not be adding new grads to their team.
Do not send multiple emails!
If you don't hear from them, we recommend applying anyway. We encourage you to continue to reach out to prospective faculty prior to the application
due date. Remember to include your top 3 faculty choices in your applciation, even
if you haven't been in contact.
Applying
Apply here
Application Deadlines:
Fall Semester - January 15th
Spring Semester - September 15th
*Summer Semester - February 15th
* We only accept Summer Admissions in special circumstances and permission must be
secured by faculty advisors prior to applying.
Materials You Need
Below is a list of materials you will need to complete the process.
Academic Transcripts. A copy of your transcript from each college or university you have attended should
be uploaded in the online application system. You can upload unofficial copies for
your application; however, if you are selected for admission to the graduate program,
official, sealed copies of transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
should be sent at that time to the university admissions office. More information
can be found on the Utah Admissions website.
English Proficiency Test Score (For international students only).
Your official report does not have to be received by the Admissions Office by the
application deadline. However, your application cannot advance until the Admissions
Office receives your official report.
3 Professional Letters of Reference. Names and contact information for three (3) references will be requested in Apply
Yourself. At least three letters of professional references are required. The recommenders
will be contacted by email and may upload their recommendations using the U of U's
online system. It is your responsibility to make sure all three letters are submitted
before the deadline. We highly recommend that you check in the system at least a week
before the due date to see which ones are missing and then email that person directly
to remind them of the deadline. Once the deadline has passed, no letters can be submitted.
CV or Resume
Statement of Purpose. A two-page personal statement outlining your background, research interests (including
possible faculty research advisors), goals, and reasons for applying to our graduate
program.
Faculty of Choice.
List 3 faculty advisors of choice (failure to list faculty advisor(s) may lesson your
chance of being accepted into the program).
Writing Sample (Optional): There is an option to submit a writing sample. Writing samples could be a research
paper, professional publication, etc.
Payment. Credit card for application fee
Just because you paid, does not mean your application has been submitted. After you pay, there is an additional step you need to do in order to complete the
process to submit your application.
Application Wavier Code: Codes are granted through the graduate advisor pending faculty
approval.
After Applying
All applicants will be notified of their acceptance or non-acceptance into the program
after the review process is complete.
For Fall:
First round offer letters are sent in February.
Subsequent offer letters are sent in March & April.
Non-acceptance notifications are sent out via the electronic system by the end of
April.
Once Accepted
U of U Admitted Grads Next Steps (university level)
Your Graduate Advisor will reach out to you to discuss next steps with the department.
Visit our Current Graduate Students Webpage
Apply to EDGES
Once you have received an offer, we encourage you to apply for the EDGES Fellowship
Program. Talk to your prospective faculty advisor before applying.
The EDGES fellowship program seeks to increase success for graduate students in STEM
fields, to enrich the academic environment for the campus community, and to broaden
the STEM workforce.
EDGES Fellows receive a monetary award (up to $10,000 per fellow) and participate
in supported cohort-based activities.
For more information, visit EDGES (Enhancing Diversity & Graduate Excellence in Science) Fellows.
